entries.title: Russia hits Ukrainian train shortly after Boris Johnson and top European officials leave station
entries.snippet: The former UK PM said "I don't know what warped logic drove Putin to blow up a stationary Ukrainian locomotive on the Polish border this morning".

entries.title: Trump downplays warnings of AI risks, citing rivalry with China
entries.snippet: The US president said "negative forces" were airing concerns about "things that won't happen".

entries.title: Questions mount over what an AI 'slowdown' would look like
entries.snippet: While pacing AI development might sound like a quick fix, it is far from an easy solution.

entries.title: Swedish party blocs tied after Sunday vote, projections say
entries.snippet: A partial count by Sweden's election authority projected that left-wing opposition bloc would win a one-seat majority.

entries.title: Six dead, 130 missing after Indonesian ferry capsizes in Java Sea
entries.snippet: Ships and helicopters are searching for those missing from the Virgo Transport 8 ship, which had encountered bad weather.

entries.title: Turkish police detain dozens in raids on gay bars and homes of LGBTQ+ activists
entries.snippet: Human rights groups in Turkey have accused the government of using a family- values campaign to target the LGBTQ+ community.

entries.title: Iran war reshapes Brics ties but also exposes divisions
entries.snippet: Brics members agree they need a new global order but it's harder to answer what should replace it and how to get there.

entries.title: Trump says he will remove all Irish whiskey tariffs as he ends two-day visit
entries.snippet: Whiskey distilled in the Republic of Ireland faces the standard 15% tariff which applies to EU goods entering the US.

entries.title: Legendary Canadian boxer George Chuvalo dies aged 89
entries.snippet: The heavyweight champion took on the likes of Muhammad Ali and Joe Frazier, and was known for never once getting knocked out or knocked down.

entries.title: US congressman swims to safety after his plane is forced to land on a lake
entries.snippet: The small plane carrying Rep Tom Tiffany had a mechanical issue that forced the pilot to make an emergency landing on a Wisconsin lake.

entries.title: They lost their jobs after posting about Charlie Kirk, but some have no regrets
entries.snippet: Some people fired in the wake of Kirk's assassination have won big settlements from employers, others have had to start over from scratch.

entries.title: Afghan woman deported from US in first use of 'alien terrorist' court
entries.snippet: The legal US resident was never charged with a crime, but was deported due to her family links to terrorism.

entries.title: Russians seek answers over hundreds missing after Ukraine's 2024 incursion
entries.snippet: Officials say more than 300 Russians remain missing after the 2024 Kursk offensive, but no-one really knows the true figure.

entries.title: Dramatic insider warnings over AI fall flat with some in Silicon Valley
entries.snippet: A recent spate of stark warnings about the dangers of AI has been met with scepticism by executives and investors.

entries.title: Best friends for decades - until a DNA test revealed they were sisters
entries.snippet: Meena Geltink and Minal Tijssen were adopted from orphanages in Mumbai in the 1980s and grew up in the Netherlands.

entries.title: Critics celebrate Céline Dion's 'high-stakes' comeback show in Paris
entries.snippet: The iconic Canadian singer kicked off her long-awaited comeback show in Paris on Saturday, after a six-year hiatus due to health issues.

entries.title: Trump's comments on a united Ireland may have targeted audience across the Atlantic
entries.snippet: Nobody could have predicted that today's main global headline would be Trump's desire to see a unified Ireland.

entries.title: Céline Dion fans prepare for comeback concert in Paris
entries.snippet: Fans of the Canadian singer greeted her as she left her hotel on Saturday.

entries.title: How global trade and oil prices could be hit by Houthi advance
entries.snippet: Yemen's Houthis have seized territory near the Bab al-Mandab Strait - a key trade gateway for oil and global shipping.

entries.title: Has Trump won over voters with his midterm convention?
entries.snippet: The BBC's North America editor Sarah Smith breaks down the main takeaways from the first-ever Republican convention held in the middle of a US presidential term.

entries.title: Pennsylvania says an unvaccinated woman has died from measles-related complications
entries.snippet: Pennsylvania has announced its third measles-related death in less than three weeks. A local coroner says the 40-year-old woman was unvaccinated.

entries.title: Trump downplays calls for AI slowdown
entries.snippet: President Trump said there were "negative forces" predicting things that he says won't happen.

entries.title: Can Gulf states and Iran negotiate the Strait of Hormuz without the U.S.?
entries.snippet: Dania Thafer of the Gulf International Forum weighs in on previously scheduled talks between Iran and Gulf states. Shortly before this interview aired, Oman announced that the talks were postponed.

entries.title: Wisconsin congressman survives emergency plane landing, swims to safety
entries.snippet: Wisconsin Congressman Tom Tiffany escaped a sinking plane and swam to shallow water after an emergency landing in a lake. Tiffany and the pilot called 911 from on top of the plane.

entries.title: Actor Tatyana Ali is advocating for Black and Indigenous maternal health
entries.snippet: Actor Tatyana Ali says her healing journey after a traumatic childbirth has inspired her advocacy for Black maternal health, including support for midwives, doulas and other birth workers.

entries.title: Politics chat: Trump's $5,000 promise to voters, Vance invokes Charlie Kirk
entries.snippet: Following the midterm convention in Dallas, President Trump's $5,000 campaign promise has generated attention, but not belief. And, Vice President JD Vance characterizes Democrats as extremists.

entries.title: From fracking to data centers: Hearing from people on both sides of the opposition
entries.snippet: NPR's Ayesha Rascoe speaks with environmentalist, Bill McKibben, and public relations specialist, Frank Maisano, about opposition to industrial development projects like fracking and data centers.

entries.title: Can you imagine a universe without a new 'Star Trek' on the horizon?
entries.snippet: As Star Trek celebrates its 60th birthday, the long-running franchise is also grappling with the challenges of timing and technology. "Its audience is aging," says Strange New Worlds star Anson Mount.

entries.title: Indonesian passenger ship overturns, sparking search for at least 129 missing
entries.snippet: Indonesian rescuers said about 130 passengers and crew are missing after a ferry carrying more than 240 people sank in bad weather in the Java Sea on Sunday.

entries.title: How a young woman was recruited to ISIS — and how she eventually escaped
entries.snippet: A young Canadian mother shares her memories of being an ISIS bride, and her harrowing escape from the extremist group.

entries.title: Trump downplays the need to check AI development and says he doesn't want to cede edge to China
entries.snippet: While acknowledging the need for some regulation, Trump provided no specifics about potential rules and attributed warnings about the technology moving too quickly and with little oversight to "negative forces" he did not identify.

entries.title: Inside a Philadelphia barbershop, Black men debate their political past and future
entries.snippet: Although Black men vote overwhelmingly Democratic, even small shifts in their support can help swing razor-thin elections. They are often some of the most scrutinized but least understood voters, a blind spot that political strategist Khalil Thompson wants to fix.

entries.title: House Speaker Mike Johnson says Trump's $5,000 'dividend' needs congressional approval
entries.snippet: Trump made the unusual pitch at the party's midterm convention in Dallas last week, promising a "Trump Dividend" if voters keep the GOP in power on Capitol Hill.

entries.title: Partial returns show close race between Sweden's conservative government and left-wing opposition
entries.snippet: Exit polls from public broadcaster SVT had initially shown the left-wing parties ahead by several percentage points but with two-thirds of the actual vote counted, the two blocs were nearly dead even.

entries.title: The secret ballot has been an article of faith in U.S. elections. That's being tested in Georgia
entries.snippet: The system's vulnerability has been drawing increased attention, with election security advocates criticizing state election officials for failing to fix it before the November elections.

entries.title: Iranian cargo ship is struck, and talks between Tehran and its neighbors are postponed
entries.snippet: The attack drew attention back to the strait after threats to shipping in the Red Sea intensified last week. Iran-backed Houthi rebels battling government forces in Yemen captured an island on the Bab el-Mandeb Strait, a crucial shipping alternative to the Strait of Hormuz.

entries.title: Rep. Tom Tiffany swims to safety after plane makes emergency landing in a Wisconsin lake
entries.snippet: Tiffany said he and the pilot remained on top of the plane in Lake Wausau until it began sinking before deciding to try and swim to shore. He said they swam about 100 to 150 feet until they reached water shallow enough to stand in.

entries.title: Trump calls on Ukraine to halt strikes on Russian diesel fuel, saying attacks are causing a shortage
entries.snippet: Ukraine has for months been targeting Russia's oil and gas industry with long-range strikes, prompting fuel rationing across the country and causing Moscow to ban diesel exports in July, one factor disrupting the global supply of diesel.

entries.title: Federal judge rules Homeland Security plan for 50% FEMA staffing cuts was unlawful
entries.snippet: The issue of the FEMA staffing was part of a much larger lawsuit filed by the American Federation of Government Employees and other labor groups, pushing back on efforts by the Trump administration to slash the federal workforce.

entries.title: Fighting in Yemen intensifies, and Houthis launch more attacks on Saudi Arabia
entries.snippet: The Yemeni government vowed to send more forces to the Red Sea coast after conceding a "painful" defeat last week when Houthis captured the port city of Mokha and an island on the Bab el-Mandeb Strait, a crucial shipping alternative to the Strait of Hormuz.

entries.title: Minnesota churches roiled by legal battle over ICE surveillance and right to protest
entries.snippet: Court cases involving Twin Cities churches and immigration enforcement highlight how the acrimonious debate continues to roil faith communities more than six months since the federal surge turned Minnesota into a symbol of defiance of the Trump administration's policies.

entries.title: Anthropic CEO says AI industry needs to give safety measures time to catch up
entries.snippet: "I believe that if slowing down bought us even an extra year or two before models reach critical levels of capability, and we used that time to advance alignment, we could greatly reduce the risk that something goes seriously wrong," Dario Amodei said.

entries.title: AP analysis: Justice Department went after protesters for felony assault, but juries and judges were unconvinced
entries.snippet: The Associated Press' analysis focused on arrests made during protests last summer and fall in LA, Chicago, Portland and Washington, D.C. — cities with significant protests where President Donald Trump sought to or successfully deployed the National Guard.

entries.title: Trump touches a nerve while in Ireland by saying reunification would be 'fantastic'
entries.snippet: At a meeting with Irish Prime Minister Micheál Martin in Dublin, Trump said he would love to see the reunification of the Republic of Ireland with the United Kingdom's Northern Ireland.

entries.title: Saudi Arabia has few options as it faces mounting threats from Iran and its allies
entries.snippet: A lightning advance by Houthi rebels threatens a crucial Red Sea shipping route. Drone attacks blamed on Iraqi militias have forced the closure of a major pipeline, and Iran is still disrupting the Strait of Hormuz.

entries.title: BRICS leaders voice concern over Middle East, condemn unilateral sanctions at India summit
entries.snippet: The meeting, which included Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian, voiced concern over "deliberate attacks" on civilian infrastructure and peaceful nuclear facilities under the U.N. atomic energy agency's safeguards.

entries.title: Trump asks Smithsonian to install George Washington statues and exhibit
entries.snippet: Trump asked for an exhibit beginning now and continuing through Feb. 22, 2032, the 300th anniversary of Washington's birth. For Constitution Day on Sept. 17, Trump asked the institution to install the 11-foot statue of Washington featured at the recent Freedom 250 IndyCar race in

entries.title: Where have all the Atlantic hurricanes gone? El Niño might bring record slow storm season
entries.snippet: On Saturday, 2026 set a record for the longest a season has begun without a storm that has reached winds of 74 mph to qualify as a hurricane — at least in the satellite era, said Nick Novella, a meteorologist at the government's Weather Prediction Center.

entries.title: Attack that closed key Saudi pipeline is blamed on Iran-backed militias in Iraq
entries.snippet: Though an umbrella group of Iran-backed militias in Iraq denied their involvement, Iraq's government confirmed the attacks had originated from its territory, pledged to investigate and dismissed two senior officials.

entries.title: Man arrested in death of Tasia Fortune, woman found hanging from tree in Mississippi
entries.snippet: The state medical examiner's office determined Thursday evening that the death was a homicide, Brackney said, allowing police to execute the warrants they already had on hand.

entries.title: DW
entries.snippet: News, Analysis and Service from Germany and Europe - in 30 Languages

entries.title: Sweden election 'very close' as left bloc claims tight lead
entries.snippet: The left-wing opposition is narrowly ahead, but it will be "very close," Social Democrat leader Andersson said. The far-right Sweden Democrats surprisingly lost ground.

entries.title: Germany's Zverev wins US Open in golden year
entries.snippet: Alexander Zverev has won the US Open for the first time, defeating Ben Shelton in the final. It is Zverev's second Grand Slam win of 2026 after a long wait for his first title, but controversy still hangs over him.

entries.title: Turkey: 162 arrested in LGBTQ+ raids
entries.snippet: Turkish authorities have arrested at least 162 people in a weekend crackdown on the country's LGBTQ+ community. Ankara says police raids on gay bars and other venues are aimed at protecting family values.

entries.title: Ukraine, Poland say Russia hit Warsaw-bound passenger train
entries.snippet: The strike hit a locomotive of a passenger train headed to Warsaw with reports that senior Western figures were at the station shortly before the attack.

entries.title: Russians on the Goethe-Institut: 'Hostage to politics'
entries.snippet: Canceled language exams, disrupted plans to study in Germany and the disappearance of an important cultural link: DW users shared how the closure of Germany's Goethe-Institut in Russia has affected their lives.

entries.title: Croatia: 'Monster' fire triggers evacuation on Brac island
entries.snippet: A rapidly spreading wildfire threatened homes and tourist accommodations on the Croatian island of Brac, with firefighters battling the blaze overnight.

entries.title: Vanuatu ferry capsize leaves one dead, 30 missing
entries.snippet: Rescue efforts have been slow after a South Pacific inter-island ferry sank in bad weather on Friday. An investigation has already begun into negligence on the part of the operator.

entries.title: Indonesia rescuers search for 130 people after ferry sinks
entries.snippet: The ship was carrying over 240 people in the Java Sea when it ran into bad weather. Officials say six people have died and 130 are still missing.

entries.title: A Romani artist in Hungary reclaims his identity
entries.snippet: Norbert Olah is an artist. He's also Romani. For a long time, he avoided making his ethnic background a theme of his art for fear of being pigeonholed. Then it became his focus.

entries.title: France: Attack ruled out in train derailment
entries.snippet: More than 40 were injured when a train derailed between Rouen and Caen in Normandy, northwest France, on Friday evening. Investigators say there is "no indication" the incident was deliberate.

entries.title: Anthropic boss Dario Amodei calls for AI slowdown
entries.snippet: Elon Musk and OpenAI chief Sam Altman say they agree with Amodei's view that safety measures need time to catch up to AI's rapid development, after a recent hacking incident by AI agents.

entries.title: Baghdad confirms attack on Saudi pipeline came from Iraq
entries.snippet: Saudi Arabia has said it will not retaliate and wants Iraq to "take the necessary measures." Baghdad is under pressure from the United States to rein in Iran-backed militias.

entries.title: Why are European banks moving gold out of United States?
entries.snippet: The Netherlands and France have moved their gold out of US vaults. Part of the reason is fears about the reliability of the US, but equally important is the need to keep gold closer to home in the event of a crisis.

entries.title: Ukraine: Several killed in series of Russian strikes
entries.snippet: Local authorities said several civilians were killed and dozens more wounded across Ukraine by Russian strikes. Meanwhile, the Kremlin has rejected Volodymyr Zelenskyy's proposal to meet with the Russian leader in Miami.

entries.title: Bulgaria: Fire at factory making munitions for Ukraine
entries.snippet: Bulgarian authorities are investigating a fire at a munitions factory for links to an explosion at a similar facility in August. Arms maker EMCO says no human error was involved, as investigators look at sabotage.

entries.title: Trump visits Ireland, says unification would be 'fantastic'
entries.snippet: US President Donald Trump's trip to Ireland to watch a golf tournament has also included meetings with leaders there.

entries.title: Uganda lays 'boy king' Oyo to rest amid succession row
entries.snippet: Uganda has buried King Oyo Nyimba, who was crowned in the Tooro Kingdom in 1995 aged just 3. His death at 34 has triggered a dispute over a successor, as rumors abound of possible heirs born out of wedlock.

entries.title: BRICS summit leaders urge 'maximum restraint' in Middle East
entries.snippet: The joint declaration at the BRICS 2026 summit expressed 'deep concern' over hostilities in the Middle East. China's President Xi Jinping said the Iran war was not in the bloc's interest.

entries.title: Russian GRU spies behind failed Leipzig attack: reports
entries.snippet: A German newspaper has cited reports tying a failed attack at Leipzig Airport to Moscow's GRU military intelligence agency. One suspect's ties to GRU were known when he entered the country, yet he was not surveilled.
